    Is Shohei Ohtani playing in the World Baseball Classic 2026?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, Shohei Ohtani played for Team Japan in the 2026 World Baseball Classic (WBC) as a designated hitter, focusing on hitting rather than pitching to manage his workload and avoid overexertion before the MLB season, a decision made in agreement with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He was a key offensive threat, but did not take the mound for Japan during the tournament, even as they were eliminated in the quarterfinals.

      Ohtani prioritized his offensive duties, contributing as one of Japan's most dangerous hitters.

      Who was the first baseball player to make $1,000,000 a year?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Pitcher Nolan Ryan was the first MLB player to sign a contract averaging over $1 million per year, signing a four-year, $4.5 million deal with the Houston Astros in 1979, a landmark contract that ushered in the era of massive player salaries in professional sports. He became the first to guarantee a seven-figure annual income, quadrupling his previous salary with the Angels.
       
      Key Details 
      • Player: Nolan Ryan
      • Team: Houston Astros
      • Date: November 19, 1979
      • Contract: Four years, $4.5 million ($1.125 million average per year)
      This deal broke the $1 million-per-season barrier, making Ryan the highest-paid player in baseball and setting a precedent for future big-money contracts, even though he was making only $200,000 with the Angels the year prior.

        How much are tickets to the World Baseball Classic?
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        World Baseball Classic ticket prices vary greatly, from as low as $3 for some pool games to hundreds or even thousands for premium seats and later rounds, with prices depending on the teams, venue (like Miami or Houston), and stage of the tournament, with semifinals and finals costing significantly more. Early rounds have cheap options, while quarterfinal, semifinal, and championship tickets, especially for popular teams like the USA or Dominican Republic, see prices jump, starting in the $100s and climbing quickly.
         
        Factors Influencing Price
        • Tournament Stage:
          Pool play is cheapest, followed by quarterfinals, then semifinals, and finally the championship game, which is the most expensive. 
        • Teams Playing:
          Games featuring popular teams (USA, Japan, Dominican Republic) or rivalries drive prices up. 
        • Venue & Seat Location:
          High demand for games in Miami (semis/finals) or Houston (quarterfinals) leads to higher costs, especially for good seats. 
        Sample Price Ranges (as of early 2026)
        • Early Pool Games:
          Some could be found for under $10, with even Brazil games starting around $3-$5 in Houston and Miami. 
        • Quarterfinals:
          Prices often started around $100-$150 but quickly went to $200+ for better seats. 
        • Semifinals:
          Starting prices could be $200-$250+, with some seats over $2,000. 
        • Championship:
          Starting prices could range from $200-$300+, with averages well above that. 
        Where to Buy
        You can find tickets on major resale sites like Ticketmaster, Vivid Seats, SeatGeek, StubHub, Gametime, TickPick, or TicketNetwork.

          Where is the 2026 WBC being played?
          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          The 2026 World Baseball Classic is being held across four host cities: Miami, Florida; Houston, Texas; Tokyo, Japan; and San Juan, Puerto Rico, with pool play in these locations and quarterfinals/semifinals in Miami and Houston, culminating in the championship game in Miami. The tournament runs from March 5-17, 2026, featuring 20 nations battling in pools, with teams like Japan, USA, Puerto Rico, and the Dominican Republic hosting and playing key games. 
          This video shows the atmosphere in Miami for a quarterfinal game:
          39s
          MLB
          YouTube · Mar 13, 2026
          Host Cities & Venues: 
          • Miami, USA: loanDepot park (Pool D, Semifinals, Championship).
          • Houston, USA: Minute Maid Park/Daikin Park (Pool B, Quarterfinals).
          • Tokyo, Japan: Tokyo Dome (Pool C).
          • San Juan, Puerto Rico: Hiram Bithorn Stadium (Pool A).
          Key Dates: 
          • Tournament Dates: March 5–17, 2026.
          • Pool Play: Early to mid-March.
          • Semifinals & Finals: Mid-March in Miami and Houston.
